title: The new goalkeeper
summary: Hugo has never played in goal, but his team has nobody else on the day of the final.
paragraphs: On the morning of the final, the phone rang at Hugo's house. It was the {{coach}}. "Our goalkeeper has broken his arm," he said. "You're tall and you're brave. Can you play in goal?" Hugo had played football for six years, but always as a defender. He said yes before he had time to think.

The match started at ten. The other team was strong and fast, and their best player kicked the ball very hard. In the first five minutes Hugo {{dropped}} the ball twice. Luckily, his defenders kicked it away. His hands were shaking.

At half time the score was 0–0. The coach sat next to him. "Stop thinking about your hands," he said. "Watch the player's feet. The feet tell you where the ball is going." In the second half, Hugo tried it. He watched the feet, and he started to understand the game in a new way.

With two minutes left, the referee gave a {{penalty}} to the other team. Their best player put the ball on the spot. Hugo looked at his feet. The player's left foot pointed to the right. Hugo jumped right, and the ball hit his hands and went over the bar.

The match ended 0–0, and Hugo's team won on penalties. His friends {{lifted}} him onto their shoulders. The next week the old goalkeeper came to training with his arm in plaster. "I hear you were good," he said, smiling. "Don't get used to it. I'll want my place back."

coach.meaning: a person who trains a sports team

penalty.meaning: a free kick at the goal, given because of a foul

lifted.meaning: moved someone or something up into the air

questions.question: Why did Hugo play in goal?
options: The usual goalkeeper had broken his arm.
The coach was angry with him.
questions.explanation: The coach called to say the goalkeeper had broken his arm.

questions.question: What advice did the coach give at half time?
options: Kick the ball as far as possible.
Watch the player's feet, not your hands.
questions.explanation: He told Hugo to watch the player's feet because they show where the ball is going.

questions.question: How did Hugo stop the penalty?
options: He closed his eyes and jumped.
He watched the player's foot and jumped right.
questions.explanation: The player's left foot pointed to the right, so Hugo jumped right.

questions.question: What did the old goalkeeper say?
options: He wanted Hugo to play in goal every week.
He was going to stop playing.
He would want his place back.
He was angry that Hugo played.
questions.explanation: Smiling, he said he would want his place back.
